messages:
Sam: Customer (acct: acme-inc) reports streaming responses that truncate ~2-4s before completion and are counted as 5xx on our side. They see billed tokens but no final chunk, unhappy about cost. sample request_id: r-9a8b7c6d.
Jess: ugh. Any gateway logs or upstream traces?
Sam: pasted logs from edge:

```
[2026-03-15T14:02:33Z] req=r-9a8b7c6d state=streaming sent_tokens=420 last_event=chunked_write error=connection_reset_by_peer
[2026-03-15T14:02:33Z] gateway: wrote chunk (len=1024)
[2026-03-15T14:02:33Z] gateway: client FIN received before trailer; closing with 499-like accounting
[2026-03-15T14:02:33Z] meter: mark_as_5xx candidate=true reason=unexpected_halfclose
```

Mike: thanks. Looks like client closed with FIN rather than waiting for final zero-length chunk. If our heuristic treats that as an upstream failure we might mark 5xx.
Priya: do we have repro steps? which client SDK?
Sam: customer uses a custom WebSocket->HTTP proxy (internal) that funnels streaming replies to browser; they say Chrome aborts connection if parent tab reloads. Hard to repro.
Jess: quick triage: ask customer for a tcpdump or curl reproducer. Also check if our gateway sees `RST` vs `FIN` — that changes classification.
Sam: asked for pcap. customer sent small tcpdump. I ran it locally: client sends FIN right after last data, but no trailing `0\r\n\r\n` chunk.
Mike: that matches: chunked transfer expects a terminal zero-length chunk. If proxy strips trailers or buffers and then closes socket, we can end up noting incomplete stream. Our current metering sometimes flips to 5xx to avoid underbilling; conservative.
Priya: can we add a temporary exception for r-9a8b7c6d to avoid billing dispute while we investigate?
Jess: yes put a credit and open support ticket. Also file an infra bug to refine heuristic: only mark 5xx if gateway/edge reported write error (EPIPE/EINVAL) plus no final chunk AND upstream reported error.
monitoring-bot: Created incident INC-2026-314 for streaming-truncation-high-error-rate (priority: P2).
Mike: small repro I used to simulate:

```
# generate a chunked response without terminal chunk then close
( echo -e "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\nContent-Type: text/plain\r\n\r\n4\r\ntest\r\n" ; sleep 0.1 ) | nc -l 8080
# then client connects and we close immediately without sending "0\r\n\r\n"
```

Jess: nice. Could also reproduce with `curl --no-buffer` and a small Python server that `conn.shutdown(socket.SHUT_WR)` early.
Sam: customer proxy shows a pattern: it flushes buffers then calls `close()` without sending terminal chunk. They said it's an old proxy lib.
Priya: next steps: (1) credit the invoice for the disputed runs (ticket S-4821), (2) recommend customer patch or upgrade proxy to send final chunk, (3) change our classification so FIN-without-final-chunk does not auto-count as 5xx unless kernel-level write error present, (4) instrument gateway to record `final_chunk_seen=true/false` for better analytics.
Jess: assign Mike for infra PR (heuristic change) and Priya to own support followups. Sam will send draft customer-facing note.
Mike: will open infra PR and include a canary that flips behavior only for streaming endpoints for 48h. Also add logging field `terminal_chunk` in traces.
Sam: customer reply: ":thumbsup: thanks, will try to update proxy. pls keep us posted on credits."
Priya: noted, marking resolved for now — keeping incident open until metric drops. :eyes:
